s: At December 31, 2014 XAGRID/AGRYLIN was approved in 47 countries . 16 PLENADREN Adrenal insufficiency (AI) is a rare, chronic and potentially fatal endocrine disorder characterised by failure in the production of the hormone cortisol.

AI affects less than 4.5 in 10,000 people in Europe 1,2 , but can lead to serious, life-threatening conditions such as cardiovascular, malignant or infectious diseases, as well as disorders which impact on health and quality of life.
The many symptoms of AI include fatigue, anorexia, weight-loss, fever, muscle weakness, abdominal pains, dizziness and headaches.
To survive, AI patients need replacement therapy with glucocorticoids (usually hydrocortisone) and because it is a chronic condition, they require this life-saving therapy throughout their lives 3 .
